argument_summary: Certification should be treated as only narrowly supportable on the existing admissible record. The admissible evidence supports the direction of release because the current build clears aggregate launch readiness and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance supports deployment with explicit documentation of evaluation results, limitations, and ongoing monitoring. The same record also shows a current telehealth discharge planning regression below the warning threshold and does not show approved mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure text. The overbroad claim is not that the release is cleanly compliant today; the narrower claim is that certification can at most be defended as caveated if the certification packet is treated as the place where the current subgroup weakness is expressly recorded as a limitation, rather than relying on prior approval or the informal monitoring comment.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost basis is needed to resolve this packet. The supportable position is based on risk-weighted interpretation of the admissible governance record, not on external cost pressure.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not permit prior approval or an informal monitoring note to substitute for current-release evidence, reviewed mitigation, or required disclosure. On this record, a clean compliant finding is not well supported. A narrower policy reading is available: aggregate readiness and rehearsal performance support certification directionally, but only with an explicit caveat that the current subgroup weakness must be understood as a disclosed limitation in the governing certification record. If the auditor is not prepared to treat the certification packet as that record, the appropriate treatment is not broad compliance but a caveated posture rather than escalation based solely on the aggregate pass evidence.
concessions: The current telehealth discharge planning slice regressed below the warning threshold.
The record does not contain reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language for that regression.
Prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and eval batch and cannot satisfy the current-release requirement.
The informal monitoring comment is contextual only and is not equivalent to approved mitigation or disclosure.
A fully unqualified compliant determination is not supported on the present record.
